## What it is

Assembly preview of a standalone, handed-neutral overhead phone tower for filming a portrait reMarkable 2.

## Design notes

The tablet is shown as a grey obstacle, not a printable part. The base stays entirely behind it, two columns rise 446 mm, and the fitted iPhone cradle sits approximately 466 mm above the desk. Print one base, four 5.1 mm mast pins, four masts, two print-in-place cam collars, one boom, one cradle locking pin, one retaining clip plus a spare, and either the fitted or universal cradle. Integral 5.2 mm dowels in the base enter the lower mast sockets. Each cam collar spans the seam between a lower and upper mast; its quarter-turn D-cam removes the sideways rocking that remains around the round pins and holds the collar in position. The boom prints with its socket collars and integral 5.2 mm alignment dowels upward, then flips over so the collars capture the mast tops and its dowels enter their upper sockets. One elastic band retains the phone in the fitted cradle (two for the universal cradle); no metal fastener is required.

The exact camera height is intentionally generous and may be reduced after a live framing test. The phone mount slides sideways so the selected rear lens is centered.

## Don't

Do not add tablet-side supports; the empty left and right edges are deliberate for both writing hands. Do not treat the grey tablet envelope as printable geometry. Do not permanently glue the mast joints before checking the camera framing. Do not increase the mast pins to remove wobble; 5.1 mm is the confirmed production pin and the cam collars carry the clamping job. Do not force a cam by bending its finger tab; release its print bridges by pushing upward from below first. Do not restore the M6 hardware requirement; the printed locking pin and clip are the standard cradle interface.
